top.line: Lovable with SHarness, and the trojanised extension
top.para: A tampered extension ran with the editor's permissions; a policy row refuses each step and two rows run today, but SHarness is Linux-only and binds no editor yet; Lovable's Git sync brings the local work into a SHarness shell, with secrets left in Lovable.

in-short.para: The tampered extension; what it did; the host was backdoored; Lovable in its cloud; the local half in a shell; a row for every step; not here, not yet.

incident.para: From Cursor's notice: versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 in its marketplace on 29 October, collecting machine details and variable names, trying an SSH backdoor and persistence; sources differ on version, user count and marketplace, and none says who.

point.para: The agent did not misbehave; extensions run with the editor's own permissions, so the boundary must sit outside the process, set before it starts.

stop.para: Each step has a refusing row: workspace-only writes and the network door run today on Linux; keys in a door and a launcher around the editor are design; so not today.

today.para: On Linux, run workspace extensions in a dev container whose policy is translated from SHarness; everywhere, keep fewer secrets where extensions run.

lovable.para: Lovable builds and hosts in its cloud; its two-way Git sync brings the local loop to a SHarness shell that writes the workspace and reaches only named sites, with production secrets kept in Lovable.

limits.para: SHarness would not have stopped this; it is early; the Lovable workflow is untested; the incident details are as reported; my interest.

sources.para: My message and the post, Cursor's notice, Geordie AI's advisory, StepSecurity's report, Microsoft's and Lovable's documentation, and sharness.ai.
